frontmatter.title: Introduction
frontmatter.description: PraxisAPP is a free practice API platform — real backends, no keys, no site login.

body:
# Introduction

PraxisAPP gives you production-shaped HTTP surfaces so you can learn, prototype, and validate client integrations without scaffolding a backend from scratch.

You get auth, ecommerce, social, chat, todos, public datasets, and HTTP utilities — all documented here and callable from the [playground](/playground).

## What you get

- **No API keys** for public practice routes — hit them and inspect responses immediately
- **Auth-backed modules** when you need JWT/session behaviour (register, login, refresh)
- **Consistent response envelopes** across domains so clients can share parsers
- **OpenAPI as source of truth** — the interactive [API Reference](/docs/api) is generated from the same spec

## Base URL

**Production**

```bash
https://praxis-api-kjrf.onrender.com
```

Routes live under `/api/v1`. For local development, point `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRAXIS_API_URL` at your local API in `.env`.

## How to use these docs

1. Start with [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) for a health check and first `GET`
2. Read [Authentication](/docs/authentication) before calling protected app routes
3. Follow the [guides](/docs/guides/first-request) for request patterns and domain maps
4. Open the [API Reference](/docs/api) when you need exact schemas, status codes, and Try It

## Spec & version

- OpenAPI: [`/openapi.yaml`](/openapi.yaml)
- API version: **1.3.1** (see [Changelog](/docs/changelog))

frontmatter.title: Authentication
frontmatter.description: Register, login, and attach JWTs for Praxis app domains (ecommerce, social, chat, todos).

body:
# Authentication

Public datasets are open. App domains (users, ecommerce, social, chat, todos) expect authenticated sessions.

## Register

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://praxis-api-kjrf.onrender.com/api/v1/users/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"demo","email":"demo@example.com","password":"Password1!"}'
```

## Login

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://praxis-api-kjrf.onrender.com/api/v1/users/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"demo","password":"Password1!"}'
```

Store the access token from the response (field names follow the OpenAPI schemas in the [API Reference](/docs/api)).

## Calling protected routes

Send the bearer token on subsequent requests:

```bash
curl -s https://praxis-api-kjrf.onrender.com/api/v1/ecommerce/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

## Refresh

Use the refresh endpoint when access tokens expire — see **Authentication** in the [API Reference](/docs/api) for the exact payload and status codes.

## Practice tips

- Prefer disposable local credentials; seed/reset helpers exist for development only
- Never commit real tokens; guides use placeholders like `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- Validate auth flows in the [playground](/playground?domain=apps) before wiring a client

frontmatter.title: Errors
frontmatter.description: How Praxis signals failures — HTTP status codes and the shared JSON envelope.

body:
# Errors

## Read both layers

1. **HTTP status** — transport-level signal (`4xx` client, `5xx` server)
2. **Envelope** — when present, check `success`, `statusCode`, and `message`

```json
{
  "data": null,
  "message": "Unauthorized request",
  "statusCode": 401,
  "success": false
}
```

Exact payloads vary by route — always confirm examples in the [API Reference](/docs/api).

## Common statuses

| Status | Meaning in practice |
|--------|---------------------|
| `400` | Validation or malformed body/query |
| `401` | Missing or invalid credentials |
| `403` | Authenticated but not allowed |
| `404` | Unknown resource or path |
| `409` | Conflict (duplicate registration, state clash) |
| `429` | Throttled — see [Rate limits](/docs/rate-limits) |
| `5xx` | Server or dependency failure |

## Kitchen-sink status drills

Force specific codes when testing client error handling:

`GET /api/v1/kitchen-sink/status-codes/{code}`

## Debugging checklist

- Confirm base URL and path prefix (`/api/v1`)
- Confirm `Content-Type` on bodies
- Confirm `Authorization` on protected routes
- Compare your payload to the OpenAPI example for that `operationId`

frontmatter.title: API usage
frontmatter.description: Headers, response envelopes, pagination, and conventions shared across Praxis domains.

body:
# API usage

## Base path

Most product routes live under `/api/v1/...`. System probes (`/health`, `/live`, `/ready`, `/version`) sit at the server root — see the [API Reference](/docs/api).

## Headers

| Header | When |
|--------|------|
| `Accept: application/json` | Prefer JSON responses |
| `Content-Type: application/json` | JSON request bodies |
| `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | Protected app routes |

## Response envelope

Successful and many error responses follow a shared shape:

```json
{
  "data": {},
  "message": "…",
  "statusCode": 200,
  "success": true
}
```

Treat `success` and `statusCode` as first-class signals; do not assume every `4xx` body is unstructured.

## Pagination

List endpoints commonly accept `page` and `limit` query parameters. Values are often typed as strings in OpenAPI — pass `"1"`, `"10"` (or numeric strings via your client). Always confirm the operation schema in the reference.

## Idempotency & verbs

- Prefer `GET` for reads and public fixtures
- Use `POST` for creates and auth actions
- Use `PATCH` / `PUT` for updates where documented
- Use `DELETE` for removals — kitchen-sink and danger-zone routes can be destructive; keep them local

## CORS

The practice API is intended for local and demo clients. If the browser blocks a cross-origin call, confirm the API CORS config and that you are targeting the URL in `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRAXIS_API_URL`.

frontmatter.title: Working with domains
frontmatter.description: Map Praxis public, apps, and kitchen-sink surfaces to the playground and OpenAPI tags.

body:
# Working with domains

Praxis groups routes into practice surfaces. Use this map to pick a starting point, then deep-dive in the [API Reference](/docs/api).

## Public

Ready-to-hit datasets — users, products, geo, quotes, and business-shaped collections (companies, invoices, orders, …).

- Playground: [/playground?domain=public](/playground?domain=public)
- OpenAPI tags: Public APIs, Geo APIs

## Apps

Authenticated product modules:

| Domain | Typical base | Playground |
|--------|--------------|------------|
| Authentication / users | `/api/v1/users` | [apps](/playground?domain=apps) |
| Ecommerce | `/api/v1/ecommerce` | [apps](/playground?domain=apps) |
| Social media | `/api/v1/social-media` | [apps](/playground?domain=apps) |
| Chat | `/api/v1/chat-app` | [apps](/playground?domain=apps) |
| Todos | `/api/v1/todos` | [apps](/playground?domain=apps) |

Read [Authentication](/docs/authentication) before calling protected ecommerce/social/chat routes.

## Kitchen sink

HTTP utilities for status codes, cookies, redirects, and request inspection — useful for edge-case clients, not product stories.

- Playground: [/playground?domain=kitchen-sink](/playground?domain=kitchen-sink)
- OpenAPI tag: Kitchen Sink

## Operations & danger zone

System health/version tags are for ops checks. **Danger Zone** and seeding helpers are development-only and can wipe or reshape local data — never point them at a shared environment you care about.

## Next

Browse every operation in the [API Reference](/docs/api), filtered by tag in Scalar’s sidebar.

frontmatter.title: Making your first request
frontmatter.description: Hit a public Praxis endpoint with cURL, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python.

frontmatter.title: Quickstart
frontmatter.description: Confirm the API is up, then make your first public GET in under a minute.

body:
# Quickstart

## 1. Run the API

Use the live API for docs examples, or run `PRAXIS_API` locally and switch `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRAXIS_API_URL` in `.env`.

## 2. Health check

```bash
curl -s https://praxis-api-kjrf.onrender.com/health
```

Expect a JSON envelope with `success: true` and operational status fields.

## 3. First public request

Public collections do not require authentication:

```bash
curl -s "https://praxis-api-kjrf.onrender.com/api/v1/public/randomusers?page=1&limit=5"
```

## 4. Try it in the browser

- [Playground](/playground?domain=public) — fire live requests with domain presets
- [API Reference](/docs/api) — OpenAPI-backed Try It console

## Next steps

- [Making your first request](/docs/guides/first-request) — JS, TypeScript, cURL, and Python
- [Authentication](/docs/authentication) — register and login for app domains
- [Working with domains](/docs/guides/domains) — public vs apps vs kitchen-sink

frontmatter.title: Rate limits
frontmatter.description: Fair-use expectations for the Praxis practice API — no invented quotas.

body:
# Rate limits

Praxis is a **practice and prototyping** API. There is no marketed public SLA and no guaranteed global quota advertised in the OpenAPI spec.

## What that means

- Do **not** assume unlimited throughput in shared or hosted deployments
- Treat aggressive parallel scraping as abuse even when no `429` is returned locally
- Prefer reasonable client pacing (tens of requests per second is already more than a tutorial needs)

## If you receive `429`

Back off exponentially, reduce concurrency, and cache public fixtures locally when you are iterating on UI.

## Production systems

When you leave the sandbox, design rate limiting, auth, and quotas deliberately. Praxis teaches client shape — it is not a substitute for your production edge.

See also [Errors](/docs/errors) for status handling patterns.

frontmatter.title: SDKs
frontmatter.description: Praxis has no official SDKs yet — use standard HTTP clients and the playground.

body:
# SDKs

There are **no official Praxis language SDKs** today. That is intentional for a practice API: you should wire real HTTP clients the same way you will against production services.

## Recommended approach

| Language | Typical stack |
|----------|----------------|
| JavaScript / TypeScript | `fetch`, Axios, ky |
| Python | `httpx`, `requests`, `urllib` |
| Shell | cURL, HTTPie |

## OpenAPI-generated clients

Generate typed clients from [`/openapi.yaml`](/openapi.yaml) with open-source generators (openapi-generator, openapi-typescript, etc.) if you want stronger typing. Keep the YAML as the source of truth — do not fork a second API definition.

## Interactive practice

- [Playground](/playground) — fire live requests without leaving the site
- [API Reference](/docs/api) — Scalar Try It with the same OpenAPI document

When first-party SDKs ship, they will be listed here and versioned in the [Changelog](/docs/changelog).
